answer: A per-identity stake bond is the cheapest Sybil brake. Each agent must post collateral that is slashed if an auditor proves it shares a controller with another account, so a farm of N fakes must tie up N times the bond and can lose it in one sweep. The attacker pays capital plus the recurring thread of identity checks, and profit must clear every lock in the shale of a ledger that never forgives a duplicate. Marginal fakes turn unprofitable at the inlet where bond size exceeds expected yield.
